*Bochen Yang,Lianlei Shan*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: PearlVLA offers a novel Vision-Language-Action approach that enhances action generation efficiency by integrating deliberation in the latent space of a vision-language model while optimizing the refinement process through a new RL framework.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the trade-off between efficient action generation and explicit deliberation in current VLA models, enhancing both performance and computational efficiency.

Method: PearlVLA separates VLM representations into visual grounding and latent planning branches, using a lightweight latent world model for iterative plan refinement and employing Causal Refinement-Grouped Process-Reward RL for optimizing this process.

Result: PearlVLA achieves state-of-the-art performance on the LIBERO benchmark, indicating its effectiveness in balancing efficiency and deliberation in action generation.

Conclusion: The proposed framework successfully integrates latent space deliberation and achieves high-performance action generation, addressing existing VLA model limitations.

Abstract: Current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models face a trade-off between efficient action generation and explicit deliberation. Directly decoding actions from vision-language backbone representations enables low-latency control, whereas explicit reasoning through textual chains, pixel-level subgoals, or action search can improve planning but incurs substantial latency and computational cost. We propose PearlVLA, a VLA framework that moves deliberation into the latent space of a vision-language model (VLM). PearlVLA separates VLM meta-query representations into a fixed visual grounding branch and an iterative latent plan branch. At each refinement round, a plan-conditioned world query probes a lightweight frozen latent world model for an action-free future observation latent, which is fed back to guide plan refinement. A future-guided RefineNet then applies scheduled residual updates to progressively refine a coarse semantic draft into a fine-grained latent action plan. The refined plan after K rounds is then decoded in parallel into an action chunk for low-latency execution. We further introduce Causal Refinement-Grouped Process-Reward RL to optimize the latent refinement process with rewards from longer-horizon imagined futures induced by latent plan edits. Empirical evaluations on the LIBERO benchmark demonstrate that PearlVLA achieves state-of-the-art performance among existing methods.

</details>


### [205] [SPARK: Low Latency Single-Camera 3D Pose Estimation for Autonomous Racing using Keypoints](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17936)
*Dominic Ebner,Markus Lienkamp*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: SPARK is a novel monocular pose-estimation algorithm for autonomous racing that provides fast and accurate detection of participants using a single camera, outperforming existing LiDAR and camera methods while ensuring low latency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need for quick detection of participants' movements in autonomous racing to ensure safe, collision-free trajectory planning against non-cooperative opponents.

Method: SPARK employs keypoint detection with a single camera to achieve long-range, high-accuracy pose estimation while utilizing optimized YOLO models and fixed geometry for efficiency.

Result: SPARK outperforms state-of-the-art monocular detection algorithms and demonstrates lower latency compared to LiDAR and other camera detection methods during evaluations on real-world data.

Conclusion: The developed SPARK algorithm significantly enhances detection speed and accuracy in autonomous racing, offering a practical solution for real-time monitoring of other participants.

Abstract: In autonomous racing, fast detection of other participants' movements is required to plan safe, collision-free trajectories with non-cooperative opponents. LiDAR detection is inherently slower and harder to deploy on edge devices than vision methods, causing delayed detections that limit object tracking performance during high-dynamic maneuvering. Utilizing monocular 3D detection enables an easy-to-deploy, low-latency detection of other participants on the racetrack. We present SPARK, a single-camera pose-estimation algorithm for autonomous racing using keypoint detection. It achieves long-range detection with high accuracy, exceeding the performance of state-of-the-art monocular camera detection algorithms while maintaining lower latency. By employing well-optimized YOLO models and leveraging the fixed geometry in the autonomous racing domain, the algorithm also exhibits low latency and resource usage. We evaluate the performance of our approach on real-world autonomous racing data and compare it to state-of-the-art LiDAR and camera detection algorithms. The source code is available at: https://github.com/TUMFTM/SPARK-camera-det

</details>


### [206] [ThinkingVLA: Interleaved Vision and Language Reasoning for Robotic Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17937)
*Tianyi Lu,Hui Zhang,Zijie Diao,Junke Wang,Shengqi Xu,Xingyao Lin,Guojin Zhong,Ziyi Ye,Peng Wang,Zuxuan Wu,Yu-Gang Jiang*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: ThinkingVLA enhances Vision-Language-Action models by integrating chain-of-thought reasoning and a unified architecture for effective cross-modal reasoning and action planning, outperforming existing methods in long-horizon tasks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need for reasoning-intensive capabilities in VLA tasks, particularly in handling long-horizon objectives that current models cannot efficiently address.

Method: ThinkingVLA employs a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture that integrates forward and inverse chain-of-thought reasoning to enable seamless subgoal decomposition and spatial anticipation, predicting visual states and inferring necessary actions.

Result: Extensive experiments show that ThinkingVLA surpasses state-of-the-art baselines in performance, especially on long-horizon manipulation tasks, highlighting its efficacy in bridging visual and textual reasoning for action generation.

Conclusion: ThinkingVLA's unified architecture significantly advances the capabilities of VLA models, particularly in reasoning-intensive scenarios, demonstrating heightened effectiveness in practical applications.

Abstract: Most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models map observations directly to actions without explicit reasoning, limiting their capacity for reasoning-intensive long-horizon tasks. To address this, existing approaches adopt Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning to enable subgoal decomposition and spatial anticipation. However, those methods lack a unified architecture for effective cross-modal reasoning and fail to explicitly include inverse reasoning ability based on the target state. We argue that manipulation planning naturally decomposes into prediction, anticipating the next visual state, and inverse dynamics, inferring the actions to reach it. Bridging both requires a unified autoregressive architecture that interleaves textual and visual reasoning in a single generation process. We propose \textbf{ThinkingVLA}, a generative model that realizes this decomposition within a unified Mixture-of-Transformers architecture. ThinkingVLA consists of a forward CoT that identifies the immediate subgoal and guides the visual forecasting; the predicted image then serves as the target state, grounding an inverse CoT that reasons about spatial relationships and action intent based on the predicted image; and the final action is generated conditioned on this full reasoning context. Extensive experiments on simulation and real-world benchmarks demonstrate that ThinkingVLA consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, with particularly large gains on long-horizon manipulation tasks.

</details>


### [207] [LAGO Policy: Latency-Aware Asynchronous Diffusion Policies with Goal-Directed Collision-Free Planning for Smooth Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17982)
*Guowei Shi,Xupeng Xie,Yiming Luo,Jian Guo,Jun Ma,Boyu Zhou*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: LAGO Policy enhances diffusion-based visuomotor policies by improving smoothness and safety in execution through integrated trajectory optimization and collision avoidance mechanisms.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Address the issues of jerky motions and collisions in diffusion-based visuomotor policies during asynchronous inference in real-world manipulation tasks.

Method: LAGO Policy proposes a unified framework combining trajectory optimization with diffusion policies, incorporating latency-aware classifier-free guidance and predicting interaction goals from demonstrations for collision-free planning.

Result: Real-world experiments show that LAGO Policy achieves smooth, collision-free execution with high success rates in complex manipulation tasks.

Conclusion: The integration of trajectory optimization enhances the performance of visuomotor policies, leading to reliable robotic manipulation.

Abstract: Diffusion-based visuomotor policies deployed with asynchronous inference often exhibit inter-chunk discontinuities and lack explicit mechanisms for obstacle-aware execution, leading to jerky motions and collisions that hinder reliable manipulation in real-world scenes. To address these issues, we propose LAGO Policy, a unified asynchronous action-generation framework that integrates trajectory optimization with diffusion policy for smooth and safe execution. LAGO Policy improves inter-chunk consistency via latency-aware classifier-free guidance conditioning on future actions. It further enables goal-directed collision-free trajectory planning by predicting a task-relevant interaction goal from demonstrations. Finally, spatial-temporal trajectory optimization refines the actions to be executed for low-jerk and feasible motion. Extensive real-world experiments demonstrate that LAGO Policy achieves smooth collision-free execution with high task success across challenging manipulation tasks. Project Website: https://lago-policy.github.io/

</details>


### [208] [Uncertainty Quantification for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18043)
*Ralf Römer,Maximilian Seeliger,Saida Liu,Ben Sturgis,Marco Bagatella,Daniel Marta,Andreas Krause,Angela P. Schoellig*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: This paper introduces a method for quantifying epistemic uncertainty in vision-language-action models (VLAs) to enhance their reliability and adaptability in non-stationary environments, proposing the SAVE framework for efficient fine-tuning with fewer expert demonstrations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Many vision-language-action models perform well in robotic manipulation but lack confidence quantification which is crucial for reliable real-world applications.

Method: The authors derive a method leveraging velocity-field disagreement (VFD) from a small ensemble to quantify epistemic uncertainty, using this for failure detection and active fine-tuning of VLAs.

Result: VFD provides better-calibrated uncertainty estimates predictive of performance, excels in failure detection, and enables uncertainty-guided data acquisition leading to at least 22% fewer required samples than standard methods.

Conclusion: The study demonstrates that improving epistemic uncertainty quantification enhances failure awareness and adaptation for flow-based VLAs.

Abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) combine vision-language backbones with expressive generative action heads trained via flow matching on large-scale robotic datasets. Despite their strong empirical performance in robotic manipulation, VLAs lack mechanisms to quantify confidence in their predictions and to detect when their actions may be unreliable. This presents a critical limitation for real-world deployment in non-stationary environments, where models inevitably encounter scenarios outside their pretraining distribution and may fail without warning. To address this, we derive an efficient method for quantifying epistemic uncertainty in flow-matching models by leveraging velocity-field disagreement (VFD) across a small ensemble. We successfully use this uncertainty estimate for failure detection during deployment and active fine-tuning of flow-based VLAs. To this end, we propose SAVE, a framework for uncertainty-guided active multitask fine-tuning that reduces the number of costly expert demonstrations required to adapt VLAs to new tasks. Through extensive experiments on the LIBERO benchmark, we demonstrate that VFD yields better-calibrated uncertainty estimates predictive of downstream performance, that VFD achieves strong performance in detecting failures, and that uncertainty-guided data acquisition with SAVE requires at least 22% fewer samples than baselines. In summary, our work shows that quantifying epistemic uncertainty in flow-based VLAs improves both failure awareness and adaptation. Project website: tum-lsy.github.io/uq_vla/.

</details>


### [209] [A Hybrid Optimization Framework for Grasp Synthesis under Partial Observations](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18053)
*Wenzheng Zhang,Fahira Afzal Maken,Tin Lai,Fabio Ramos*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: A hybrid grasp synthesis framework combining Energy-Based Models and Iterative Closest Point methods yields improved grasp success rates.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To develop a robust method for grasp synthesis that effectively utilizes both data-driven learning and geometric optimization for partially observed point clouds.

Method: A hybrid approach integrating a learning-based Energy-Based Model with an analytical Iterative Closest Point technique, driven by Stein Variational Gradient Descent for grasp refinement.

Result: Achieved a 60.9% average success rate on 67 objects from 5,360 attempts, significantly outperforming competing methods: AnyGrasp (31.1%), Grasp Pose Detection (48.4%), and AS-ICP (56.6%).

Conclusion: The proposed approach effectively combines learning and optimization, enhancing grasp synthesis performance beyond traditional methods.

Abstract: We propose a hybrid grasp synthesis framework that combines a learning-based Energy-Based Model (EBM) with an analytical Iterative Closest Point (ICP) method to generate robust grasps from partially observed point clouds. The learned energy function acts as a prior within a Stein Variational Gradient Descent (SVGD) framework, guiding iterative refinement of grasp configurations. Evaluated on 67 objects with 5,360 grasp attempts, our method achieves an average success rate of 60.9\%, outperforming AnyGrasp (31.1\%) and Grasp Pose Detection (48.4\%) and AS-ICP (56.6\%). These results highlight the strong generalization ability of our approach and demonstrate how combining data-driven learning with geometric optimization addresses the limitations of either strategy in isolation.

</details>


### [210] [EAGG: Embodiment-Aligned Grasp Generation via Geometry-Aware Graph Conditioning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18092)
*Wanhao Niu,Qiyan Ke,Yuan Sun,Hao Sun,Jie Xu,Muyuan Ma,Ruiqi Hu,Fuchun Sun*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: EAGG is a novel embodiment-aligned grasp generator that improves cross-end-effector grasp generation by using a topology-aware end-effector graph and iterative geometry injection for enhanced geometry awareness, achieving high success rates across multiple embodiments.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need for a generalized grasp generator that performs effectively across various end-effectors and object types, overcoming limitations of existing static or fixed-embodiment models.

Method: EAGG employs a topology-aware end-effector graph and an embodiment-specific low-dimensional control space, using a frozen cognition backbone for geometry-aware token generation, complemented by iterative geometry injection for dynamic adaptation during sampling.

Result: EAGG achieves a 56.17% average success rate on the MultiGripperGrasp benchmark, near specialized training performance, and significantly reduces median contact distance through iterative geometry injection.

Conclusion: Aligning embodiment structures within a common generator enhances cross-end-effector grasp generation, indicating that embracing differences is more beneficial than suppressing them.

Abstract: Cross-end-effector grasp generation seeks a unified model that generalizes across objects and across embodiments ranging from parallel grippers to dexterous end effectors. Existing grasp generators are typically designed for a fixed embodiment or encode embodiment identity with a static descriptor, which weakens transfer when topology, actuation coupling, and contact geometry differ substantially. We present EAGG, an embodiment-aligned grasp generator that represents each embodiment with a topology-aware end-effector graph and an embodiment-specific low-dimensional end-effector control space. A frozen end-effector-cognition backbone converts the current articulated state into geometry-aware tokens that act as a reusable morphology prior, and iterative geometry injection refreshes these tokens throughout sampling so that conditioning remains synchronized with the evolving end-effector geometry. On the MultiGripperGrasp benchmark, EAGG reaches 56.17% average success across six training end effectors, remaining within 1.10 percentage points of specialized training while preserving transfer to finetuning and zero-shot end effectors. Iterative geometry injection further reduces the pooled median contact distance from 0.239 cm to 0.189 cm. These results show that cross-end-effector grasp generation is strengthened by aligning embodiment structure inside a shared generator rather than suppressing embodiment differences. Code is available at https://github.com/wanhaoniu/EAGG.

</details>


### [211] [WireCraft: A Simulation Benchmark for Industrial DLO Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18097)
*Chongyu Zhu,Ramy ElMallah,Hyegang Kim,Zachary Tang,Jiachen Rao,Artem Arutyunov,Seungyeon Ha,Chi-Guhn Lee*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: The paper presents WireCraft, a simulation benchmark for manipulating Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs) in industrial settings, addressing gaps in existing benchmarks by providing configurable task assets and shared evaluation protocols.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The complexity of manipulating DLOs in industrial contexts due to their infinite-dimensional configuration space and deformation during contact requires better benchmarks for policy development and comparison.

Method: WireCraft offers three task families for DLO manipulation, supports two physics models, and employs reinforcement learning, imitation learning, and vision-language-action policies to evaluate performance under shared metrics.

Result: Privileged state-based reinforcement learning achieved over 82% success in task completion, revealing that while the tasks are viable, challenges remain, particularly in the contact-rich scenarios for vision-based methods.

Conclusion: The benchmark and tools could enhance research in DLO manipulation but highlight significant challenges for current learning methods, especially in vision-based approaches.

Abstract: Deformable Linear Objects (DLOs), such as wires and cables, are central to industrial assembly. Unlike rigid objects, whose state is captured by a 6-DoF pose, DLOs have an infinite-dimensional configuration space and deform continuously under contact with grippers, fixtures, and the workspace, making them a demanding benchmark for general dexterous manipulation. Despite their importance, policy development and comparison remain difficult: existing benchmarks are often tied to specific hardware setups, lack modular and customizable task assets, or study generic deformable-object tasks without the fixtures relevant to real-world industrial wire manipulation. Few benchmarks align simulation, real-world data, and shared evaluation protocols. To bridge this gap, we introduce WireCraft, a simulation benchmark for industrial DLO manipulation with configurable difficulty and assets, spanning three task families: connector insertion, clip routing, and channel seating. It supports two complementary DLO physics models, articulated and deformable, and the trajectories come from both simulation and a physical UR5. We benchmark reinforcement learning (RL), imitation learning (IL), and vision-language-action (VLA) policies under shared metrics. Privileged state-based RL solves a representative setting in each task family with over 82\% success, confirming the tasks are well-posed. For connector insertion, however, the transition from reaching the socket to contact-rich alignment remains a key bottleneck for vision RL, IL, and VLA policies. These results indicate that industrial DLO manipulation, though tractable under privileged state, remains an open challenge for current vision-based learning. The benchmark, data, and tools will be open-sourced upon acceptance.

</details>


### [212] [Qwen-RobotNav Technical Report: A Scalable Navigation Model Designed for an Agentic Navigation System](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18112)
*Jiazhao Zhang,Gengze Zhou,Hale Yin,Yiyang Huang,Zixing Lei,Qihang Peng,Haoqi Yuan,Jie Zhang,Xudong Guo,Xiaoyue Chen,An Yang,Fei Huang,Junyang Lin,Dayiheng Liu,Jingren Zhou,Zhuoyuan Yu,Jingyang Fan,Zhixuan Liang,Pei Lin,Ye Wang,Anzhe Chen,Kun Yan,Xiao Xu,Jiahao Li,Lulu Hu,Minying Zhang,Shurui Li,Wenhu Xiao,Shuai Bai,Xuancheng Ren,Chenxu Lv,Chenfei Wu,Xiong-Hui Chen*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: Qwen-RobotNav is a scalable navigation model designed for flexible observation strategies across different tasks like instruction following and autonomous driving, showing state-of-the-art results.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To create a navigation model adaptable to varying task demands while using a unified perception-planning backbone.

Method: Introduced a parameterised interface with multiple task modes and controllable observation parameters, trained on 15.6M samples using vision-language co-training to enhance robustness and performance.

Result: Qwen-RobotNav achieved state-of-the-art results in navigation benchmarks and demonstrated effective scaling and zero-shot generalisation capabilities.

Conclusion: The model's design allows for dynamic task management and complex behaviour composition, underlining its potential as a foundational component for advanced agentic systems.

Abstract: Agentic navigation systems require a base navigation model whose observation strategy can be externally reconfigured at inference time, because instruction following, object search, target tracking, and autonomous driving share the same perception-planning backbone yet demand fundamentally different strategies for consuming the visual stream. We present Qwen-RobotNav, a scalable navigation model built on Qwen-RobotNav that addresses it through a parameterised interface with two complementary dimensions: multiple task modes that select the navigation behaviour, and controllable observation parameters (e.g., token budget, per-camera weights) that govern how visual history is encoded. With training-time randomization over all parameters, Qwen-RobotNav is robust to any inference-time configuration requiring zero architectural modification to the Qwen-RobotNav backbone. We train Qwen-RobotNav on 15.6M samples; co-training with vision-language data prevents the collapse into reactive action-sequence mappers observed in trajectory-only training. The parameterised interface also makes Qwen-RobotNav a natural building block for agentic systems: for long-horizon scenarios, an upper-level planner decomposes goals into sub-tasks and dynamically switches Qwen-RobotNav's task mode and context strategy mid-episode, composing complex behaviours from repeated calls to the same model. Extensive experiments show that Qwen-RobotNav sets new state-of-the-art results across major navigation benchmarks. The model exhibits favourable scaling from 2B to 8B parameters, with joint multi-task training developing a shared spatial-planning substrate that transfers across task families, and demonstrates strong zero-shot generalisation to real-world robots across diverse environments.

</details>


### [213] [Beyond Failure Recovery: An Engagement-Aware Human-in-the-loop Framework for Robotic Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18189)
*Jiaying Fang,Joyce Yang,Zhanxin Wu,Bohan Yang,Tapomayukh Bhattacharjee*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: The paper introduces Engagement-aware MPC (E-MPC), a method for improving user engagement in human-robot interactions, particularly in caregiving contexts, by balancing interaction frequency with workload constraints.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Many human-robot interaction methods treat users as mere tools, leading to dispassionate engagement, particularly in caregiving scenarios where users may have mobility limitations that restrict their interaction with robots.

Method: E-MPC utilizes a user interaction dynamics model to proactively manage engagement levels throughout a task, rather than relying solely on failure-driven interactions while ensuring the robot completes its tasks successfully.

Result: The approach was validated through simulations and a real-world study, demonstrating that E-MPC enhances user experience for users with mobility limitations while maintaining effective task performance.

Conclusion: E-MPC offers a promising framework for fostering meaningful engagement between users and robots in caregiving settings by balancing the need for user interaction with their cognitive workload.

Abstract: Conventional human-in-the-loop approaches typically involve users only when a robot encounters failure or uncertainty, treating humans primarily as tools for improving robot performance. However, in many human-centered robotics settings, interaction should support engagement by keeping users involved in decision-making rather than limiting them to failure-driven interventions. This is particularly compelling in physical caregiving, where mobility limitations can reduce users' ability to intervene or modulate the robot's behavior in the moment. As a result, failure-driven interaction policies may relegate users to passive observers for long stretches of the task. For example, a user with mobility limitations may feel less engaged when being continuously and passively fed by a robot. At the same time, overly frequent interaction can be tiring and increase the user's workload.
  To address this trade-off, we propose Engagement-aware MPC (E-MPC), a user-engagement-aware method that plans interaction to maintain engagement while respecting a workload constraint. E-MPC leverages a user interaction dynamics model that captures how user engagement evolves as a function of both the frequency and type of interaction. Rather than requesting input only when difficulties arise during task execution, the robot proactively considers the user's preferred level of engagement throughout the task, balancing autonomy and interaction while ensuring task success. We evaluate E-MPC in simulation with several ablations and baseline comparisons. Results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach across diverse user personas. In addition, we conduct a real-world user study with participants with emulated mobility limitations on a robot-assisted bite acquisition system, showing that E-MPC improves user experience while maintaining task success.

</details>


### [214] [EBench: Elemental Diagnosis of Generalist Mobile Manipulation Policies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18239)
*Ning Gao,Jinliang Zheng,Xing Gao,Haoxiang Ma,Hanqing Wang,Yukai Wang,Jiantong Chen,Zanxin Chen,Shujie Zhang,Mingda Jia,Xuekun Jiang,Zihou Zhu,Xinyu Li,Shuai Wang,Hao Li,Wenzhe Cai,Yuqiang Yang,Xudong Xu,Zhaoyang Lyu,Yao Mu,Tai Wang,Jiangmiao Pang,Jia Zeng,Weinan Zhang,Chunhua Shen*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: EBench is a benchmark for evaluating the capabilities and generalization of mobile manipulation policies across 26 tasks, revealing distinct profiles among state-of-the-art models.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need to assess mobile manipulation policies beyond success rates to gain deeper insights into their performance and capabilities.

Method: EBench includes diverse manipulation tasks annotated along five capability dimensions and four generalization dimensions; it evaluates multiple state-of-the-art models.

Result: State-of-the-art models show differing capability profiles despite similar success rates, with specific strengths and weaknesses identified in tasks and generalization abilities.

Conclusion: EBench provides diagnostic signals for improving generalist manipulation models by identifying performance variances across capabilities and generalization factors.

Abstract: We present EBench, a simulation benchmark that diagnoses generalist mobile manipulation policies beyond a single success-rate scalar. EBench comprises 26 diverse and challenging manipulation tasks annotated along 5 capability dimensions and 4 generalization dimensions. We evaluate state-of-the-art generalist manipulation models including $π_0$, $π_{0.5}$, XVLA, and InternVLA-A1, and reveal that models with near success rates exhibit strikingly different capability profiles: $π_{0.5}$ achieves the highest test success rate and the best train--test retention, whereas InternVLA-A1 dominates mobile manipulation but collapses on dexterous tasks, and XVLA exhibits strengths on a disjoint set of atomic skills compared to other policies. Beyond capability profiling, EBench analyzes the generalization ability from 4 representative perspectives, identifying the impact of different distribution shift factors. The results reveal strengths and weaknesses of models behind an overall score. We hope this benchmark offers a broad set of diagnostic signals to guide iteration on generalist manipulation models.

</details>


### [215] [Visual Verification Enables Inference-time Steering and Autonomous Policy Improvement](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18247)
*Mingtong Zhang,Dhruv Shah*

Main category: cs.RO

TL;DR: The paper introduces VERITAS, a framework for improving robot policies through inference-time verification and self-improvement, without needing additional training.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To enable robots to learn from experiences and improve their performance in real-world applications.

Method: The proposed VERITAS framework uses a pre-trained robot policy as a generator and a gradient-free visual verifier to assess actions during inference, enhancing policy performance.

Result: Inference-time verification consistently shows better performance than standard generalist policies, and fine-tuning on verified trajectories leads to significant performance improvements.

Conclusion: Inference-time verification is an effective approach for robot policy enhancement, allowing for scalability and efficiency comparable to expert demonstrations without the need for human intervention.

Abstract: Robots deployed in the real world should learn from their experience and improve over time. This requires a mechanism of practicing and learning from feedback. In this paper, we propose VERITAS, a generator-verifier framework for generalist robot policies for inference-time policy steering and self-improvement. We use a pre-trained generalist robot policy as a ``generator'' and pair it with a gradient-free ``visual verifier'' that evaluates actions at inference time. This framework enables inference-time steering that improves policy performance without additional training. We demonstrate that inference-time verification consistently outperforms vanilla generalists without training on additional demonstration data. Additionally, we demonstrate that the verified rollouts provide effective supervision for offline policy improvement: policies fine-tuned on verified self-generated trajectories achieve consistent performance gains. Notably, we find that post-training with verified rollouts achieves comparable efficiency to expert demonstrations, while requiring no human interventions. Our results highlight inference-time verification as a practical and scalable mechanism for improving robotic policies during deployment.

</details>


<div id='cs.IR'></div>

# cs.IR [[Back]](#toc)

### [216] [On the Memorization Behavior of LLMs in Generative Recommendation: Observations, Implications, and Training Strategies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17276)
*Sunwoo Kim,Sunkyung Lee,Clark Mingxuan Ju,Donald Loveland,Bhuvesh Kumar,Kijung Shin,Neil Shah,Liam Collins*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: The paper addresses the limitations of LLMs in generative recommendation due to their tendency to memorize training data, particularly through one-hop memorization. It introduces a training strategy, IIRG, to enhance LLMs' ability to learn richer item relations for better recommendations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To explore the memorization problem in LLMs fine-tuned for generative recommendation and identify its impact on recommendation performance.

Method: The proposed IIRG strategy enables LLMs to learn collaborative and semantic relations among items beyond simple one-hop transitions.

Result: IIRG significantly enhances the recommendation performance of LLMs compared to standard next-item prediction, especially for users with unseen test items not represented in one-hop memorization.

Conclusion: The findings suggest that overcoming memorization can lead to improved generative recommendation outcomes, highlighting the need for models to learn deeper item-item interactions.

Abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) has emerged as a promising direction for recommender systems. Recently, large language models (LLMs) have been increasingly adopted for GR, as their rich pretrained knowledge is expected to help them generalize beyond common user behavior patterns that traditional memorization-oriented baselines can capture. However, existing LLM-based GR works largely ignore LLMs' well-known tendency to memorize, which, if present in LLMs fine-tuned for GR, would restrict their utilization of pretrained knowledge. In this work, we investigate this concern by examining one-hop memorization, where a model recommends items that are direct successors of items in the training data. We show that LLMs do this more than non-LLM-based GR models-in fact, the vast majority of their gains over GR baselines are actually on users whose target items can be predicted through one-hop memorization. We intuit that improving performance on the remaining users requires LLMs to learn richer item-item relations beyond one-hop transitions. To achieve this, we propose IIRG, a novel training strategy that teaches LLMs to capture: (1) collaborative relations derived from item co-occurrences across multiple hops in user sequences, and (2) semantic relations among items with similar themes, both of which can serve as useful recommendation signals. We show that IIRG significantly improves over LLMs trained solely with standard next-item prediction, with especially large gains for users whose test items are not covered by train-time one-hop transitions.

</details>


### [217] [RSRank: Learning Relevance from Representational Shifts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17468)
*Archit Gupta,Sai Sundaresan,Debabrata Mahapatra*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: The paper introduces a new reranking method for RAG-based systems that utilizes representational shift (RS) for relevance scoring instead of traditional heuristics and logit signals, achieving improved performance across various datasets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation is to enhance the filtering process in RAG-based systems using a principled approach to relevance scoring, overcoming the limitations of heuristic thresholds and logit signals.

Method: The method involves identifying representational shifts induced by candidate documents and utilizing a lightweight training framework to map these shifts to calibrated relevance scores, facilitating the filtering of irrelevant content.

Result: The approach shows improvements over existing state-of-the-art rerankers across diverse retrieval datasets by providing a more accurate assessment of document relevance.

Conclusion: The study concludes that leveraging representational shifts offers a robust indicator of relevance and enables effective document filtering without relying on heuristic tuning.

Abstract: As enterprises deploy RAG-based systems to provide grounded responses to user queries, reranking has become a critical component for the final filtering step that separates relevant from distracting or irrelevant documents. Existing rerankers often rely on heuristic thresholds to achieve optimal filtering. Moreover, for relevance scoring, state-of-the-art methods use a language model's logit signals, which are designed for next-token prediction, not for assessing relevance. To address these limitations, we identify a principled signal for relevance: the representational shift (RS) induced in a query's internal state when conditioned on a document. We observe that the alignment between (a) RS induced by a candidate document and (b) RS induced by an oracle document-set provides a robust indicator of relevance. Building on this insight, we introduce a lightweight training framework that learns projections mapping RS to calibrated relevance scores. Our training objectives naturally filter irrelevant content at a zero threshold, reducing dependence on heuristic tuning. Across diverse retrieval datasets, our method delivers gains over SOTA rerankers.

</details>


### [218] [Temporal Preference Optimization for Unsupervised Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17664)
*HyunJin Kim,Jaejun Shim,Young Jin Kim,JinYeong Bak*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: TPOUR is a novel unsupervised retriever that uses Temporal Retrieval Preference Optimization to improve retrieval of temporally relevant documents without requiring explicit timestamps, outperforming existing models.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the limitation of unsupervised dense retrievers in capturing temporal relevance in document retrieval when dealing with collections spanning multiple time periods.

Method: The proposed TPOUR employs Temporal Retrieval Preference Optimization (TRPO) which emphasizes preference learning in a temporal context, enhancing the retrieval of temporally aligned documents. It utilizes continuous temporal alignment through interpolation in learned time embeddings.

Result: TPOUR outperforms both unsupervised and supervised baselines in temporal information retrieval tasks, particularly showing notable improvements in nDCG@5 scores. Despite its smaller size, it significantly enhances retrieval performance on both explicit and implicit queries compared to larger models.

Conclusion: TPOUR effectively enhances the retrieval of temporally relevant documents while being more efficient than existing models, providing a practical solution for temporal information retrieval.

Abstract: Unsupervised dense retrievers offer scalability by learning semantic similarity from unlabeled documents via contrastive learning, but they struggle to capture the temporal relevance, retrieving semantically related but temporally misaligned documents-an important aspect when a document collection spans multiple time periods (e.g., retrieving documents from 2018-2025 for "Who is the president in 2019?" introduces temporal ambiguity). Existing methods rely on supervised training with explicit timestamps, which are not always feasible. We propose TPOUR (Temporal Preference Optimization for Unsupervised Retriever), which uses our novel training method Temporal Retrieval Preference Optimization (TRPO). TRPO reinterprets preference learning in the temporal dimension, guiding the retriever to favor temporally aligned documents. TPOUR further generalizes to unseen time periods via interpolation in a learned time embedding, enabling continuous temporal alignment. Experiments on temporal information retrieval (T-IR), TPOUR outperforms both unsupervised and supervised baselines. Compared to Qwen-Embedding-8B, despite being about 72.7x smaller, TPOUR Contriever improves average nDCG@5 by +4.04 (+12.15%) on explicit and +4.98 (+15.21%) on implicit queries. We provide our code at https://github.com/agwaBom/TPOUR.

</details>


### [219] [Do Generative Recommenders Deepen the Information Cocoon? A Closed-Loop Simulation with LLM-powered User Simulators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17707)
*Jiyuan Yang,Gengxin Sun,Mengqi Zhang,Lingjie Wang,Yuanzi Li,Hongxi Cui,Xin Xin,Pengjie Ren*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: This paper investigates the impact of generative recommenders on information cocoon formation, revealing they tend to encourage broader exposure than traditional recommenders, though feedback can still lead to cocooning based on tokenization and model size.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To explore the role of generative recommenders in the creation of information cocoons, which may limit users' exposure due to repeated feedback mechanisms.

Method: A closed-loop simulation framework called RecLoop was developed, utilizing LLM-driven user agents to compare two generative recommenders and two traditional baselines across multiple feedback cycles on Amazon datasets.

Result: Generative recommenders exhibit less exposure-level cocoon formation compared to traditional methods, but feedback loops can create concentration within the Semantic ID space, influenced by tokenization strategies and model scales.

Conclusion: Findings indicate that the formation of information cocoons in generative recomender systems is influenced by recommendation behaviors, item tokenization approaches, and the capacity of the models.

Abstract: Recommender systems alleviate information overload, yet repeated feedback between recommendations and user interactions can reinforce existing preferences and narrow users' exposure, forming information cocoons. While this phenomenon has been widely studied in traditional sequential recommendation, its impact on generative recommendation remains unclear. By replacing atomic item IDs with Semantic ID (SID) sequences, generative recommenders introduce a different recommendation mechanism whose role in information cocoon formation is not yet understood. To investigate whether generative recommenders deepen information cocoons, we propose \textsc{RecLoop}, a closed-loop simulation framework with LLM-driven user agents. We compare two generative recommenders and two traditional sequential baselines on two Amazon datasets across multiple feedback cycles. In addition to standard exposure-level metrics, we introduce \emph{Code-Space Structural Cocoon}, a model-level metric that measures concentration in the generated SID space. Experimental results show that generative recommenders are generally less prone to exposure-level cocoon formation than traditional baselines, preserving broader exposure diversity and slowing cross-user homogenization. However, feedback loops can still induce concentration within the generated SID space. We further find that cocoon severity depends strongly on tokenization strategy and model scale: collaborative-signal tokenization produces stronger cocoon effects than semantic tokenization, whereas larger models maintain greater code-space diversity and better retain access to niche content. These findings suggest that information cocoons in generative recommendation are shaped not only by recommendation behavior, but also by item tokenization and model capacity. Our code is available at https://github.com/Dregen-Yor/RecLoop.

</details>


### [220] [Understanding and Debugging Failures in N-Gram-Based Generative Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17721)
*Richard Takacs,Adrian Bracher,Svitlana Vakulenko*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: This paper explores failure modes in Generative Retrieval (GR) systems, proposing a taxonomy, empirically investigating ngram-based methods, and introducing a tool for analysis.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The paper is motivated by the need to understand the failure mechanisms in Generative Retrieval systems which are influenced by advancements in language models.

Method: The authors develop a taxonomy of GR failures, conduct empirical investigations on ngram methods like SEAL and MINDER, and present a web-based tool for analyzing the impact of generated identifiers on ranking.

Result: The analysis uncovers issues like ambiguous document identifiers (docids), low diversity in identifiers, and the uneven effect of certain identifiers in the ranking process.

Conclusion: The study provides insights into the shortcomings of GR systems and introduces helpful resources for the IR community to enhance their understanding and improve methodologies.

Abstract: Generative Retrieval (GR) is an emerging Information Retrieval (IR) paradigm that is motivated by increasingly capable language models. In GR, a model directly generates identifiers for relevant documents. While these systems offer unique advantages, they also introduce distinct failure mechanisms. We explore these failure modes in three contributions: (1) We present a taxonomy of GR failure modes based on GR literature. (2) We empirically investigate failure in a subset of GR: ngram-based methods, more specifically, SEAL and MINDER. Our analysis reveals common issues, such as ambiguous docids, low identifier diversity, and the disproportionate impact of specific identifiers. (3) We introduce a new web-based tool that helps the IR community analyze generated ngrams and their respective contribution to the final ranking, providing an intuitive interface to identify where such GR methods go wrong.

</details>


### [221] [Non-negative Elastic Net Decoding for Information Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17910)
*Koki Okajima,Yasutoshi Ida,Tsukasa Yoshida,Yasuaki Nakamura*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: The paper introduces Non-Negative elastic Net (NNN) decoding for improved document retrieval, addressing limitations of dense retrieval by enhancing diversity and performance.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome the limitations of dense retrieval, which often results in redundancy by selecting semantically similar documents without considering the broader corpus context.

Method: The authors propose NNN decoding, treating retrieval as a joint decoding problem where document selections reconstruct the query embedding as a sparse non-negative linear combination.

Result: NNN decoding can handle queries more effectively, particularly in corpora with correlated documents, and outperforms traditional dense retrieval in various benchmarks and metrics.

Conclusion: The paper suggests a new approach to using dense embeddings in information retrieval that enhances both diversity and performance compared to standard inner-product scoring.

Abstract: Dense retrieval has become the dominant paradigm in information retrieval, in which each document is scored against a query by the inner product of their vector embeddings, and the top-$k$ documents by score are retrieved for this query. However, since each document's score depends solely on the embedding of the query and itself, the retrieval process is oblivious to the content of the entire corpus. Therefore, dense retrieval cannot avoid selecting semantically similar documents from the corpus, which may result in a non-diverse, redundant set of retrieved documents. To this end, we approach retrieval as a joint decoding problem, in which documents are selected as a set with regard to the context of the rest of the corpus. To achieve this, we propose Non-Negative elastic Net (NNN) decoding, which selects documents whose embeddings jointly reconstruct the query embedding as a sparse non-negative linear combination.
  Our main theoretical result establishes a strict separation between dense retrieval and NNN decoding. For any corpus, every query correctly handled by dense retrieval is also handled by NNN decoding, while on corpora containing correlated documents, NNN decoding additionally handles queries that dense retrieval cannot. Experimental results indicate that applying NNN decoding to frozen embeddings trained for inner-product scoring yields consistent improvements across several benchmarks. Moreover, we introduce an end-to-end training procedure which optimizes the embeddings for NNN decoding, producing significant performance gains surpassing in all metrics and benchmarks compared to dense retrieval. Our work establishes a new paradigm for leveraging dense embeddings in information retrieval, beyond the standard practice of inner-product scoring.

</details>


### [222] [IUU+DB: Tracking Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated Fishing, Seafood Fraud, and Labor Abuse through LLM-driven Information Extraction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.18181)
*Henry Bodwell,Hong Yang,John C. Simeone,Kelvin Gorospe,Bella Sullivan,Lana Huang,Jessica Gephart,Sandy Aylesworth,Molly Masterton,Naren Ramakrishnan*

Main category: cs.IR

TL;DR: The paper introduces IUU+ to encompass broader illegal fishing activities and proposes IUU+DB, a language model system to compile a global database of such incidents for better analysis and enforcement.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the inadequacies in understanding illegal fishing beyond traditional definitions and to provide a structured method for tracking related environmental and supply chain crimes.

Method: The proposed IUU+DB system utilizes language models to analyze various documents, classify incidents, extract key data, and facilitate trend analysis and deduplication.

Result: Validation studies indicate that IUU+DB effectively organizes information, identifies hotspots, aids research and industry assessments, and supports policy enforcement.

Conclusion: IUU+DB presents a significant advancement in tracking IUU+ activities, enhancing both academic research and policy implementation for improved marine ecosystem protection.

Abstract: Illegal, unreported, and unregulated fishing (IUU) traditionally refers to fishing activities that violate applicable laws or occur in areas that lack applicable laws. We propose the term IUU+ to capture a broader suite of fisheries sector environmental and associated supply chain trade-related crimes and behaviors. Although IUU+ activity is widely recognized as a serious threat to marine ecosystems, markets, and livelihoods, a quantitative understanding of these incidents, e.g., their frequency, geography, species, actors, and patterns in the type of illicit activity, remains difficult to obtain. We propose IUU+DB, a large language model driven system for building a global incident database of IUU+ activity. The system ingests heterogeneous documents, classifies whether they describe relevant incidents, extracts key data elements such as actors, locations, species, vessels, violations, and enforcement outcomes, and supports deduplication and trend analysis. Case studies and validation results show that IUU+DB can help organize fragmented evidence, surface geographic and behavioral hotspots, support fisheries-domain specific research in academia and non-government organizations, assist source and species risk assessments for industry, and provide support for policy implementation and targeted enforcement efforts to government agencies.

</details>


<div id='cs.NE'></div>

# cs.NE [[Back]](#toc)

### [223] [ZIVARI-TLBO: A Zero-Cost Inter-Group Evaluated-Elite Relay Mechanism for Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17087)
*Pezhman Zivari*

Main category: cs.NE

TL;DR: ZIVARI-TLBO is a novel optimization algorithm that enhances a population-state controller, showing strong performance in comparisons with other methods across various dimensions and functions, though with some limitations in engineering applications.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To improve optimization performance using a grouped Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO) method with a relay mechanism for sharing elite solutions among groups.

Method: An evaluated elite relay system is introduced where elite solutions are shared in a fixed ring structure, replacing worse learners in the receiving group when advantageous, evaluated under set budgets and multiple classical functions.

Result: ZIVARI-TLBO outperformed traditional algorithms, recording impressive wins against a baseline method, but was outperformed by WOA and showed mixed results in engineering applications.

Conclusion: While ZIVARI-TLBO demonstrates potential with its innovative relay mechanism, it does not uniformly excel across all problem types, suggesting a defined scope for its applicability.

Abstract: ZIVARI-TLBO is a grouped Teaching-Learning-Based Optimization (TLBO) method that augments an existing population-state controller with a fixed inter-group evaluated-elite relay. At each scheduled event, every group offers its already evaluated elite to the next group in a fixed ring; the elite replaces the receiver's worst eligible learner only when its stored objective value is better. Because the exact relay copies an already evaluated solution and its stored fitness, it requires no additional objective-function calls. The frozen gts-v4-cm-fixed implementation is evaluated under equal 10,000-evaluation budgets on eight classical functions at dimensions 10, 30, 50, and 100, with 30 matched seeds, and on five constrained engineering problems. A direct ablation against the same grouped landscape-aware controller without relay records 728/11/221 wins/ties/losses and a rank-biserial effect size of 0.624 across dimensions. In an eight-method multidimensional comparison, WOA obtains the best average rank (2.914) and ZIVARI-TLBO ranks second (3.382); ZIVARI-TLBO significantly outperforms TLBO, MCTLBO, DE, PSO, and GWO, loses significantly to WOA, and is not significantly different from HHO after Holm adjustment. Feasibility-aware engineering results are mixed and sensitive to the current static-penalty formulation. The evidence supports a scoped relay contribution and budget-consistent information-sharing mechanism, but not universal state-of-the-art, global-convergence, engineering-dominance, or CEC superiority claims.

</details>


### [224] [Directing Open-Ended Evolution in Artificial Life via Multi-Scale Path Divergence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17091)
*Mikhail Akhtyrchenko,Mikhail I. Katsnelson,Andrey Ustyuzhanin*

Main category: cs.NE

TL;DR: This paper introduces MSPD, a new complexity metric for open-ended evolution in artificial life that quantifies the organization of heterogeneity in transition laws, linking biological dynamics to physical theories of complexity.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome limitations of black-box neural-network complexity metrics and connect artificial life systems to physical complexity theories.

Method: MSPD is defined as a scalar at the population level, computed using a windowed finite-resolution estimator that captures temporal multiscale organization of heterogeneity in transition laws.

Result: MSPD-optimized parameters yield higher complexity scores compared to random parameters; higher MSPD is linked to greater instability and frustration in biological dynamics.

Conclusion: MSPD serves as both a fitness function and analytical tool, facilitating open-ended evolution while providing a link to the physics of complexity unlike traditional black-box metrics.

Abstract: Open-ended evolution (OEE) in artificial life is typically driven by uninterpretable, black-box neural-network complexity metrics, leaving life-like systems disconnected from physical theories of complexity. We introduce MSPD (Multi-Scale Path Divergence, denoted DP ), a renormalization-group-inspired scalar that quantifies the temporal multiscale organization of heterogeneity in local transition laws. MSPD is defined at the population level as a functional of the realised trajectory and is computed as a windowed finite-resolution estimator, with consistency between the two stated as a proposition. The metric is an explicit formula and plays a dual role: as a gradient-free fitness function and as a post-hoc analytical lens on any simulation that exposes local transition laws. Empirically, MSPD-optimized parameters produce higher held-out complexity scores than matched random parameters from the same substrate. High-$H_{Delta_t}$ states correspond to states with higher instability to external interventions, so the metric tracks the biology of the underlying dynamics rather than noise. Higher MSPD corresponds to stronger scale-dependent frustration: high-complexity systems exhibit larger differences between the dynamics expressed at different spatial extents, linking MSPD directly to the frustration criterion of biological complexity in the sense of Vanchurin et al. [ 23 ]. The same protocol transfers beyond the primary Flow-Lenia substrate to Life-like cellular automata and Particle Life++, where C1, C2 and C5 all hold. A single explicit formula thus both directs open-ended evolution and provides a principled bridge to the physics of complexity that black-box drivers do not.

</details>


### [225] [Evolutionary Algorithms and Multi-Objective Minimum Spanning Trees with Limited Distinct Weight Values](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17731)
*Narges Tavassoli Kejani,Andrew M. Sutton,Frank Neumann*

Main category: cs.NE

TL;DR: This paper explores the runtime of evolutionary algorithms for multi-objective combinatorial optimization, focusing on the minimum spanning tree problem and the structure of the Pareto front under specific conditions.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The paper addresses the lack of theoretical results on the runtime of evolutionary algorithms for multi-objective combinatorial optimization problems.

Method: The authors analyze the structure of the Pareto front when edge weights have few distinct values and derive new runtime results for existing algorithms, supported by experimental data.

Result: New theoretical runtime bounds for evolutionary algorithms are established, revealing insights into the Pareto front's structure.

Conclusion: The findings enhance understanding of evolutionary algorithms' performance in multi-objective optimization settings and suggest avenues for further research.

Abstract: Evolutionary algorithms have been used for a wide range of multi-objective combinatorial optimization problems. Despite practical success, theoretical results on the runtime of evolutionary algorithms for multi-objective combinatorial problems are rather limited. One classical problem that has been investigated is the multi-objective minimum spanning tree problem for which runtime bounds have been obtained to compute all extremal corner points of the Pareto front. With this paper, we provide some more detailed insights into the structure of the Pareto front when the edge weights take on a small number of distinct values. Based on these insights, we derive new runtime results for evolutionary multi-objective algorithms and complement our theoretical results with experimental investigations.

</details>


### [226] [An Optimization Framework for Automated Assessment of Biological Plausibility of Spiking Neurons](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17853)
*Sven Nitzsche,Alexandru Ionita,Andreas Faust,Bogdan Ionescu,Juergen Becker*

Main category: cs.NE

TL;DR: The paper introduces an open-source framework for assessing biological plausibility in spiking neural models by evaluating their ability to replicate biological firing patterns.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the inconsistent definition and quantification of biological plausibility in neuromorphic computing.

Method: An automated framework evaluates neuron models by comparing their firing patterns to established biological patterns, using objective functions for optimization without prior analytical models.

Result: The framework successfully characterizes several known neuron models and a new model, demonstrating its empirical assessment capability.

Conclusion: The tool serves as a foundational step for exploring the link between biological plausibility and various performance metrics in machine learning.

Abstract: Biological plausibility is a key concept in neuromorphic computing and spiking neural networks, yet it remains inconsistently defined and difficult to quantify. In this work, we present an open-source framework for the automated assessment of biological plausibility in spiking neuron models. Our method builds on the idea of evaluating a model's ability to replicate canonical neuronal firing patterns observed in biological systems, following the classification proposed by Izhikevich. By encoding these patterns into objective functions and optimizing model parameters accordingly, our framework enables empirical assessment without requiring prior analytical modeling. Treating neuron models as black boxes, it provides a practical and flexible means of characterizing their dynamic capabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework on several established models and a previously unexplored custom model. Implemented in Python and compatible with PyTorch and the Norse library, the framework is tailored for machine learning contexts. It is intended as a starting point for systematic research into the relationship between biological plausibility and network-level performance metrics such as accuracy, energy efficiency, robustness, and adaptability.

</details>


<div id='eess.SP'></div>

# eess.SP [[Back]](#toc)

### [227] [Sensing-Native Over-the-Air Federated Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17117)
*Peiyuan Huang,Shijian Gao,Jia Yan,Georgios B. Giannakis*

Main category: eess.SP

TL;DR: Proposes a sensing-native over-the-air federated learning framework that integrates distributed sensing with efficient model training without additional overhead.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To improve the performance of over-the-air federated learning systems that face resource competition with dedicated sensing modules.

Method: Develops a framework utilizing local gradient signals for both model training and target distance estimation, while addressing inter-device interference and noise with trilateration and matched filtering.

Result: Achieves better learning and sensing performance through the proposed framework compared to existing models, backed by simulation results.

Conclusion: Demonstrates that integrating sensing capabilities into federated learning can enhance performance with optimal resource allocation and advanced communication techniques.

Abstract: Over-the-air federated learning (FL) leverages the superposition property of multiple-access channels to enable communication-efficient distributed model training. Existing integrated sensing, communication, and computation (ISCC)-enabled over-the-air FL systems typically require dedicated resources for the sensing module, inevitably compromising FL performance due to resource competition. In this paper, we propose a sensing-native over-the-air FL framework that explores built-in distributed wireless sensing capability with zero overhead per model aggregation. Specifically, the high-dimensional local gradient signals possessing favorable autocorrelation property are concurrently leveraged for target distance estimation, while the gradient statistics already required for over-the-air FL serve as a ready-made gateway to deliver locally-sensed results to the edge server for cooperative localization. To combat inter-device interference, channel fading, and communication noise, we put forth a robust trilateration-based target positioning method building upon an efficient matched-filtering-based distance estimation. Then, by explicitly characterizing the impact of imperfect model aggregation and noisy gradient-statistics transmission on the sensing-native over-the-air FL convergence, we develop a statistics-aware communication-learning co-design approach. We first derive the closed-form optimal power budgets allocated to local gradients and their statistics, based on which an efficient successive convex approximation method is proposed for receiver beamforming optimization. Simulation results show that the proposed framework simultaneously achieves superior learning and sensing performance compared to representative baselines.

</details>


### [228] [Precoding Sequence Design for MIMO Sensing with Scatterers Based on Prior Information](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17198)
*Yiming Liu,Wei Yu*

Main category: eess.SP

TL;DR: This paper addresses MIMO sensing design in the presence of scatterers, highlighting the need for full temporal sequence optimization rather than just precoding matrices due to signal-dependent interference.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To improve MIMO sensing capabilities in environments with scatterers, which alters traditional design methodologies that focus on target-only scenarios.

Method: The study formulates a worst-case BCRLB minimization problem across multiple target angles, employing constant-modulus or constant-norm hardware constraints with a max-min fractional program approach, followed by a linear transformation to derive an iterative algorithm for precoder updates.

Result: The developed algorithm shows notable improvements in estimating azimuth angles of multiple targets, achieving effective suppression of scatterer interference and enhanced target illumination through innovative sensing sequences.

Conclusion: The proposed framework successfully integrates joint precoder-combiner design and adaptive prior refinement in multi-stage sensing, offering robust solutions for MIMO sensing in complex environments.

Abstract: The presence of interfering scatterers fundamentally changes the design principle for MIMO sensing. Unlike the target-only case, where MIMO sensing sequence design reduces to optimizing the transmit sample covariance, this paper shows that scatterer-induced signal-dependent interference makes the Bayesian Fisher information depend on the full temporal precoding sequence. Consequently, for the MIMO sensing problem with scatterers using the Bayesian Cramér-Rao lower bound (BCRLB) as the objective, the entire sensing sequence must be designed explicitly, instead of just the precoding matrix. This paper considers such a precoding sequence design problem under hardware constraint for MIMO sensing for estimating the azimuth angles of multiple targets based on the prior information of both the targets and the scatterers. We formulate a worst-case BCRLB minimization across multiple target angles, yielding a max-min fractional program under constant-modulus or constant-norm hardware constraints. We further develop a constant-norm linear transform that converts the ratio objectives into linear forms, leading to an iterative algorithm with closed-form precoder updates. The framework extends to joint precoder-combiner design and multi-stage sensing with adaptive prior refinement. Numerical results demonstrate the effectiveness and the efficiency of the proposed algorithm, revealing sweeping-like beampatterns that illuminate target angular regions while suppressing interference from the scatterers.

</details>


### [229] [Gauge Freedom Optimization for Truncation Error Reduction in Inertial Navigation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17202)
*Yaakov Libero,Itzik Klein*

Main category: eess.SP

TL;DR: This paper presents the u-space methodology for improving numerical integration in inertial navigation systems, specifically addressing limitations in current techniques for unknown forcing functions.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current methods for reducing numerical integration errors in inertial navigation systems require knowledge of the forcing functions, which limits their applicability.

Method: The u-space methodology generalizes gauge freedom to systems with unknown forcing functions, deriving optimal gauges for second-order systems in closed form and for first-order systems in both closed and empirical forms.

Result: Monte Carlo simulations demonstrated consistent error reduction across various conditions and real-world datasets, particularly enhancing performance in high-grade inertial systems and aided low-cost systems.

Conclusion: The proposed u-space methodology effectively reduces truncation errors in numerical integration for inertial navigation systems, making it applicable across different sensor grades and types of systems.

Abstract: Numerical integration plays a central role in inertial navigation systems, where sensor measurements are propagated through time to obtain orientation, velocity, and position states. The accuracy of this propagation depends on the numerical integrator type, order and step-size. Prior work showed that for second-order systems with known forcing functions, the gauge freedom in the variation of parameters technique can be exploited to reduce truncation error without modifying the integrator. However, this approach requires analytical knowledge of the forcing function, limiting its applicability in real-world systems. To address this limitation we propose the u-space methodology, a novel state mapping that generalizes the gauge freedom to systems with unknown forcing functions. The optimal gauge is derived in closed form for second-order systems and in both closed and empirical form for first-order systems. The proposed approach was evaluated through Monte Carlo simulations across four forcing functions, five sensor grades, and four Adams-Bashforth orders, as well as on a real-world inertial navigation dataset. Results show consistent error reduction across all tested conditions, with the largest gains observed in the full inertial mechanization pipeline, making the approach applicable to high-grade inertial systems, where truncation error constitutes a larger share of the error budget, and to aided low-cost systems with high-rate updates, where propagation spans only short inter-update intervals.

</details>


### [230] [A Unified Analytical Nullspace-Based Least-Squares Design of the Farrow Structure](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17219)
*Deijany Rodriguez Linares,Håkan Johansson*

Main category: eess.SP

TL;DR: This paper presents a unified least-squares design for Farrow structures, improving variable fractional-delay filter implementations by accommodating mixed filter types while addressing group-delay constraints.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The paper aims to enhance the efficiency and flexibility of variable fractional-delay filters by overcoming limitations in the decoupling of linear-phase and general FIR filter branches due to group-delay constraints.

Method: It introduces a nullspace parameterization approach for the symmetry constraints of individual branches in Farrow structures, which allows for an analytical solution that supports different filter types.

Result: The proposed framework satisfies group-delay constraints that the traditional all-linear-phase method cannot meet, while reducing the number of free parameters compared to the general FIR approach.

Conclusion: The unified LS design improves upon existing methods, providing a more versatile and efficient solution for implementing variable fractional-delay filters.

Abstract: Farrow structures based on linear--phase FIR subfilters provide an efficient realization of variable fractional--delay (VFD) filters with reduced implementation complexity. While the all--linear--phase configuration admits a decoupled least--squares (LS) formulation with an analytical solution, this decoupling fails when branches of mixed types, linear--phase and general FIR, are required, as occurs when a group--delay constraint is imposed. This letter presents a unified LS design for Farrow structures via a nullspace parameterization of the per--branch symmetry constraints, yielding an analytical solution that accommodates arbitrary per--branch types. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed framework satisfies group--delay constraints that the all linear--phase approach cannot meet, while substantially reducing the number of free parameters relative to the unconstrained general FIR baseline.

</details>


### [231] [Large-scale Tunable Liquid Lens-assisted VLC Systems under Random Receiver Orientation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17247)
*Kapila W. S. Palitharathna,Constantinos Psomas,Gaofeng Pan,Ioannis Krikidis*

Main category: eess.SP

TL;DR: This paper presents a tunable liquid lens-assisted receiver design for enhancing performance in large-scale VLC systems with dynamic receiver orientations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address performance issues in VLC systems caused by random receiver orientations and dense AP deployments.

Method: An electrowetting-based TLL architecture is proposed, utilizing a mathematical model to analyze the optical channel, with three lens orientation strategies.

Result: Numerical results indicate a 57.1% reduction in outage probability with the BSR scheme compared to fixed-lens receivers under specified conditions.

Conclusion: The TLL-assisted receiver significantly improves VLC system robustness against orientation fluctuations and informs future network design.

Abstract: This paper investigates the performance of tunable liquid lens (TLL)-assisted receivers in large-scale visible light communication (VLC) systems under random receiver orientation. A simple electrowetting-based TLL architecture is proposed, capable of dynamically steering the incident optical signal toward the photodiode receiver by adjusting the orientation of the liquid interface. The proposed architecture enhances the desired signal reception while mitigating interference from neighboring access points (APs). The spatial distribution of APs is modeled using a Matérn hard-core point process, whereas receiver orientation is characterized by uniformly distributed azimuth angles and Gaussian-distributed polar angles. Furthermore, a tractable mathematical optical channel model is developed to capture the combined effects of AP/receiver locations, receiver orientation, and lens adjustment angles on the VLC channel gain. Based on this framework, three lens orientation strategies, namely best signal reception (BSR), closest LED selection, and vertical upward lens orientation, are proposed to improve system performance under dynamic receiver conditions. Using stochastic geometry tools, exact and approximate analytical expressions for the outage probability are derived for each scheme. Numerical results verify the accuracy of the developed analysis and demonstrate that the proposed TLL-assisted receiver architecture significantly improves the robustness of VLC systems under severe receiver orientation fluctuations and dense AP deployments. In particular, the BSR scheme reduces the outage probability by $57.1\%$ compared with conventional fixed-lens receivers at an AP height of $3.5$ m and AP density of $0.2~\text{m}^{-2}$. The presented analytical framework and numerical results provide useful design insights for the deployment of future TLL-assisted VLC networks.

</details>


### [232] [Robust Beamforming Design for Secure Uplink NOMA-ISAC](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17306)
*Azadeh Tabeshnezhad,Milad Tatar Mamaghani,A. Lee Swindlehurst,Tommy Svensson,Erik Ström*

Main category: eess.SP

TL;DR: The paper explores an uplink NOMA system for 6G networks that integrates communication and radar sensing, focusing on enhancing security against eavesdropping through a combined optimization approach.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the security vulnerabilities introduced by integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) in 6G networks, especially against potential eavesdroppers.

Method: A joint optimization problem is formulated, using an iterative alternating optimization algorithm to optimize receive combining vectors and transmit beamforming matrices while ensuring security.

Result: The developed solution shows fast convergence and effective resource allocation, improving both users' sum rate and BS sensing performance against eavesdropping.

Conclusion: The proposed method enhances physical-layer security in uplink NOMA systems, making it suitable for the secure implementation of ISAC in 6G mobile networks.

Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication is an important technology for sixth-generation (6G) mobile networks, enabling the joint use of communication and radar sensing within a unified system. While offering significant benefits in terms of spectral efficiency, ISAC introduces new security challenges. In particular, the joint use of resources for sensing and communication can increase vulnerability to eavesdropping and information leakage. In this paper, we study an uplink Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) system where the base station (BS) simultaneously receives user data and senses a potential eavesdropper (Eve) with uncertain location. To enhance the physical-layer security, a robust sensing signal is designed to both sense and jam Eve. We formulate a joint optimization problem that aims to maximize the users' sum rate and the BS sensing performance while maintaining security against Eve. Since the resulting optimization problem is non-convex, we develop an iterative alternating optimization (AO) algorithm that decomposes it into two tractable subproblems. In the first subproblem, the receive combining vectors are optimized in closed form using generalized eigenvalue decomposition. In the second subproblem, the transmit beamforming matrices and sensing power are jointly optimized via semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and successive convex approximation (SCA). Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our solution in terms of fast convergence and resource allocation.

</details>


### [233] [Pilot-Aided MIMO Channel Identification and Linear Deconvolution in Correlated Gaussian Noise](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17311)
*Necati Kagan Erkek,Y. Ugur Ozcan*

Main category: eess.SP

TL;DR: This paper investigates MIMO channel identification and deconvolution using pilot symbols in the presence of spatially correlated noise, revealing the impact of pilot block length and conditioning on channel estimation and data recovery.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To understand the effects of pilot symbols and noise correlation on MIMO channel identification and deconvolution performance.

Method: The study employs a $4\times4$ MIMO model under Gaussian noise, utilizing maximum-likelihood/least-squares for channel estimation and comparing mean-square error against the Cramer--Rao bound, followed by data recovery with maximum-likelihood zero-forcing and MMSE deconvolution.

Result: Long and well-conditioned pilot blocks enable the channel estimator to approach theoretical limits, while short blocks introduce limitations; MMSE regularization outperforms zero-forcing at low SNR and inaccuracy.

Conclusion: The results highlight the significance of pilot sequence design and noise management for enhanced MIMO channel estimation and data recovery.
